_about: JBL frames every implementation must build or read byte for byte. Requests marked jbltray were recorded from a Tune Flex 2 by JblTray (github.com/emperorbug46/JblTray, emperorbug46, MIT, commit 5ccf929); replies marked fajkpes were recorded from a Tune 720BT by FajkPes's JBL-Headphones-App (github.com/FajkPes/JBL-Headphones-App, commit 3f383d1, no licence: the bytes are used as facts); those marked app are built the way JBL Headphones 5.37.10 builds them, not yet seen on a device.

race._about: Airoha's RACE frames for JBL's Airoha models (docs/jbl/PROTOCOL.md section 10), built the way JBL Headphones 5.37.10 and Airoha's SDK in it build and read them; none seen on a device yet. The replies are made up in the layout the SDK reads.

segment_eq._about: Realtek's segment EQ (docs/jbl/PROTOCOL.md section 11.1), from Realtek's libDspConfig.so in JBL Headphones 5.37.10 run in an emulator outside the repo. calculate: DspConfig.calculateEq's input (Realtek band types: 0 peak) and the library's whole answer (the largest gain, two bytes; 12 bytes of module header; the stage data). writes: a curve and a design EQ (bands as Harman type, Hz, dB, Q) and the A6 frames JBL's code builds around the library's answers at 44.1 and 48 kHz, for an MTU of 512 and 185. design_harman: the design EQ as the Harman curve the earbuds report. None seen on a device yet.

airoha_peq._about: Airoha's PEQ coefficients (docs/jbl/PROTOCOL.md section 11.2), from libnative-peq.so in JBL Headphones 5.37.10 run in an emulator outside the repo with Android 17's own arm64 libc and libm: each curve's bands (Hz, dB, bandwidth in Hz), the master gain in dB, the sample rate, generateCofe's code, getCofeParam's shorts after changeRescaleCofe, and getPeakValue's figure at 44.1 kHz times 100 (as AirohaPeqMgr stores it). None seen on a device yet.
airoha_peq.serialize_about: AirohaEQSerialize.serializePEQ (type 0) as JBL's app sends it in protocol 4's EQ curve feature (0E7F) on the models whose EQ library is Airoha's: JBL's ten bands at these gains and Q (all sent as Airoha's peak, type 2), the master gain (the curve's left gain) and the model's sample rates, built from libnative-peq-serialize.so run in an emulator outside the repo.
